correctness.rationale: The radial gauge of the three-cylinder intersection follows exactly from its three defining quadratic inequalities. Six pair-equality planes cut a generic central plane into twelve sectors where only one cylinder is active. Orthogonal coordinate projection has Jacobian |n_i| on the plane, so each sector area is a mapped disk sector with exact atan2 angle. Dominated convergence covers degenerate normals. The global minimum and equality cases follow from an integrand inequality and the fact that a circle cannot be covered by finitely many isolated coordinate-axis intersections. A uniform four-zero local layer analysis yields the cubic |p|^3+|q|^3 term. This forbids a third-order Taylor polynomial. Three exact sample orientations and independent numerical radial/polygon checks of 240 and 24 generic normals (max errors <8e-10 and <9e-9) corroborate the proof. These finite checks are not the proof.

value.rationale: Central-plane section area is a natural directional invariant of the classical Steinmetz tricylinder; knowing its solid volume and surface area does not fix the area of a section at every normal. The 12-sector formula evaluates the entire normal sphere through finitely many elementary angles, the global minimum includes sharp equality classification, and the uniform cubic expansion detects an anisotropic, non-C3 slicing singularity invisible in the isotropic quadratic response. These are structural geometric statements, not a single arbitrary numerical slice or an exercise in normalization. The proof is self-contained and the verification reproducible.
